q1.question: How long does the process usually take?
q1.answer: Immigration timelines are controlled by USCIS, the immigration courts, and federal circuit schedules — not by us. A realistic estimate depends on your specific case type, current backlogs at your venue, and the completeness of your evidence. During your free consultation we'll give you a concrete timeline based on what your case actually looks like.

q2.question: What happens if my case is denied?
q2.answer: A denial is rarely the end. Depending on the filing, you may have 30 days to file a motion to reopen, an appeal to the BIA, or — in some cases — a federal petition for review at the circuit court. We explain all your options, the costs, and the odds honestly.

q3.question: Can I work while my case is pending?
q3.answer: In many situations yes — through an Employment Authorization Document (EAD, Form I-765) tied to your underlying filing. Eligibility depends on the case type and filing date. We file the EAD as part of our case packages whenever it applies.

q4.question: Do you offer payment plans?
q4.answer: Yes. Flat fees make costs predictable, and every engagement we take on comes with a written payment plan that splits the fee into manageable installments. We bill in full transparency — no surprise charges.

q5.question: Is the first consultation really free?
q5.answer: Yes. Your free consultation is a 20–30 minute conversation with an intake specialist or attorney. We listen to your story, identify the legal issues, and tell you what we'd do. You leave with a plan whether you hire us or not.

q6.question: Can you help if I don't live in Florida?
q6.answer: Yes. We represent clients in immigration courts and USCIS offices nationwide. Because immigration is federal law, your physical address does not limit who can represent you — most of our work is done remotely, with court appearances handled in person when required.

deportation-defense.title: Deportation Defense
deportation-defense.short: Full-service defense when the government files removal proceedings against you.
deportation-defense.headline: When the government comes for you, we come for them.
deportation-defense.overview1: Removal proceedings are the highest-stakes immigration matter. You are in immigration court and the government is trying to deport you. Every hearing, every filing, every piece of evidence matters.
deportation-defense.overview2: Our deportation defense practice handles every stage: initial Master Calendar, motions practice, relief applications (cancellation, asylum, adjustment), and merits hearings with cross-examination and expert witnesses.
deportation-defense.overview3: We take every case personally because the consequences are irreversible. You deserve an attorney who prepares for your hearing like it's theirs.
deportation-defense.step1Desc: We read the NTA, identify every form of relief you may qualify for, and build a ranked strategy.
deportation-defense.step2Desc: Country reports, affidavits, medical and psychological evaluations, corroborating documents from home country.
deportation-defense.step3Desc: We appear with you, enter pleadings, request relief, and lock in the merits hearing date.
deportation-defense.step4Desc: Mock hearings, witness prep, legal brief, expert declarations, and a binder that tells your story.
deportation-defense.step5Desc: We present your case in court. If the judge rules against us, we file the BIA appeal the same day.

deportation-detained.title: Deportation Defense (Detained)
deportation-detained.short: Emergency representation when your loved one is in ICE custody.
deportation-detained.headline: Out of detention first. Then we fight the case.
deportation-detained.overview1: Detention changes everything. Filings move faster, visits are restricted, and the psychological pressure on your family is enormous. We file emergency motions to get you before a judge quickly.
deportation-detained.overview2: Our detained practice combines bond work, release requests, and substantive removal defense in a single coordinated engagement — because separating them costs time you don't have.
deportation-detained.overview3: We coordinate with the detention facility, family outside, and the court to keep everyone informed and to move the case forward while you're inside.
deportation-detained.step1Desc: Same-day consultation with family. We pull A-file, identify the facility, and file EOIR-28.
deportation-detained.step2Desc: We file a bond motion and appear at the next hearing. Most of our detained clients are released within 2–4 weeks.
deportation-detained.step3Desc: Once out (or while still in), we prepare relief applications and build the record.
deportation-detained.step4Desc: Full hearing on the merits with full evidence. Client appears by VTC or in person.
deportation-detained.step5Desc: Appeal if necessary. Post-order supervision or custody challenges if applicable.

deportation-adjustment.title: Deportation Defense + Adjustment of Status
deportation-adjustment.short: Combined defense in removal proceedings plus a green card application.
deportation-adjustment.headline: Defend in court. Adjust in court. One plan, one fee.
deportation-adjustment.overview1: If you have a qualifying family relationship (immediate relative of a U.S. citizen) and you're in removal proceedings, you may be able to adjust status before the immigration judge. It is one of the most favorable outcomes possible.
deportation-adjustment.overview2: This package bundles your removal defense with the adjustment application so everything moves together. You get a coordinated record, coordinated evidence, and a single merits hearing focused on approval.
deportation-adjustment.overview3: We handle the I-130 coordination if not yet approved, the I-485 in court, the medical exam, and the interview-style merits hearing.
deportation-adjustment.step1Desc: Confirm the qualifying relationship, admissibility, and that there are no bars.
deportation-adjustment.step2Desc: If not already approved, we file and track the I-130 with USCIS in parallel.
deportation-adjustment.step3Desc: Submit the adjustment packet with the immigration court, including affidavit of support and medical.
deportation-adjustment.step4Desc: The judge conducts an interview-style hearing and grants or continues pending I-130 approval.
deportation-adjustment.step5Desc: Green card is issued by USCIS. We help with the card pickup and any follow-up filings (I-751, N-400).

cancellation-of-removal.title: Cancellation of Removal
cancellation-of-removal.short: 42A and 42B relief for long-term residents facing deportation.
cancellation-of-removal.headline: Ten years of your life, ten years of hope, protected.
cancellation-of-removal.overview1: Cancellation of removal is a discretionary form of relief for people who've lived in the U.S. for 10+ years and who have qualifying U.S. citizen or LPR relatives who would suffer exceptional and extremely unusual hardship if you were removed.
cancellation-of-removal.overview2: It is one of the hardest forms of relief to win. The hardship standard is intentionally high. Winning requires detailed, corroborated evidence and a compelling narrative that no other case replicates.
cancellation-of-removal.overview3: We prepare cancellation cases like trials — expert witnesses, psychological evaluations, country conditions, medical records, school records, and financial documentation for every qualifying relative.
cancellation-of-removal.step1Desc: Continuous physical presence, qualifying relative, good moral character, no bars.
cancellation-of-removal.step2Desc: Medical, educational, financial, community, and country-conditions evidence for every qualifying relative.
cancellation-of-removal.step3Desc: EOIR-42B and supporting brief filed with the court well ahead of the merits hearing.
cancellation-of-removal.step4Desc: Testimony from you, qualifying relatives, and experts. Cross-examination prep. Closing arguments.
cancellation-of-removal.step5Desc: If granted, LPR status. If denied, BIA appeal filed within 30 days.

master-calendar.title: Master Calendar Hearing
master-calendar.short: Individual Master Calendar appearance in immigration court.
master-calendar.headline: Don't face the judge alone.
master-calendar.timeline: Single hearing (30–45 minutes at court, preparation separate)
master-calendar.overview1: A Master Calendar is the procedural hearing where you enter pleadings, identify relief, and get the merits hearing scheduled. It's short but consequential — mistakes here limit what you can pursue later.
master-calendar.overview2: We appear with you, enter pleadings correctly, request all relief you may qualify for, and push for the best possible schedule.
master-calendar.overview3: This service is designed for clients who want a one-time Master Calendar appearance without engaging us for the full case — typically because the case is in an early or transitional stage.
master-calendar.step1Desc: Review your NTA and file to determine what relief to request.
master-calendar.step2Desc: Draft admissions, denials, and relief requests.
master-calendar.step3Desc: We appear with you, enter pleadings, and set the merits hearing.
master-calendar.step4Desc: Written summary of what happened, what was scheduled, and what to do next.
master-calendar.step5Desc: Refer back to your attorney, or convert to a full engagement with us.

individual-hearing.title: Individual (Merits) Hearing
individual-hearing.short: Full merits hearing representation on removal relief.
individual-hearing.headline: One hearing. Your life on the line. We don't improvise.
individual-hearing.timeline: Half-day to full-day hearing; 60–90 days of prep
individual-hearing.forms: Relief-specific applications, witness affidavits, legal brief
individual-hearing.overview1: The Individual Hearing (also called the merits hearing) is where your case is decided. You present evidence, testify under oath, and argue legal issues. The judge issues a decision — sometimes from the bench.
individual-hearing.overview2: We accept merits-only representation when a client has an existing attorney handling the case but needs trial-level preparation and courtroom presence. We work alongside your current counsel or solo.
individual-hearing.overview3: Our merits prep includes witness prep, mock cross-examination, expert coordination, legal brief, exhibit list, and a binder the judge can actually use.
individual-hearing.step1Desc: Review the full file, identify trial issues, and design the theory of the case.
individual-hearing.step2Desc: You and every witness rehearse direct and cross, often multiple times.
individual-hearing.step3Desc: Exhibit list, corroborating evidence, expert declarations, country reports.
individual-hearing.step4Desc: Full courtroom representation — opening, direct, cross, closing.
individual-hearing.step5Desc: Written decision review. Appeal if needed (30 days to BIA).

asylum.title: Affirmative Asylum (USCIS)
asylum.short: Affirmative asylum applications filed with USCIS.
asylum.headline: Your story belongs in the record. Told right.
asylum.overview1: Affirmative asylum is available to people in the U.S. who are not yet in removal proceedings and who fear persecution in their home country on account of race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership in a particular social group.
asylum.overview2: The case turns on credibility. Your declaration is the heart of the file. Every date, every actor, every event must be consistent and corroborated where possible. Gaps or contradictions sink cases.
asylum.overview3: We draft your declaration in Spanish first (with you), translate it, corroborate it with country reports and supporting affidavits, and prep you for the asylum interview.
asylum.step1Desc: Confirm eligibility and either meet the one-year filing deadline or fit an exception.
asylum.step2Desc: Multiple drafting sessions to produce a detailed, consistent personal statement.
asylum.step3Desc: Country conditions, police/medical records, witness affidavits. File the I-589 package.
asylum.step4Desc: Biometrics at ASC; asylum interview at the asylum office with our attorney present.
asylum.step5Desc: Grant, recommended approval, referral to court, or NOID response — we handle each outcome.

credible-fear-interview.title: Credible Fear Interview
credible-fear-interview.short: Representation for Credible Fear or Reasonable Fear interviews at a detention facility.
credible-fear-interview.headline: The interview that decides whether you get a chance at asylum.
credible-fear-interview.timeline: 7–30 days from referral; interview prep in days
credible-fear-interview.overview1: If you enter the U.S. and express fear of return, you'll be scheduled for a Credible Fear Interview. Passing the interview means you get placed in removal proceedings where you can pursue asylum. Failing means removal, often within days.
credible-fear-interview.overview2: The interview covers identity, route of travel, and the reasons you fear persecution. Asylum Officers are trained to look for inconsistencies. One short, scared, poorly prepared answer can end the case.
credible-fear-interview.overview3: We prep you remotely or in person at the detention facility, identify the protected ground, practice the narrative, and represent you by phone during the interview.
credible-fear-interview.step1Desc: Same-day family consultation, facility identification, retainer signed.
credible-fear-interview.step2Desc: Protected ground identification, narrative drafting, question practice.
credible-fear-interview.step3Desc: Telephonic representation during the interview itself.
credible-fear-interview.step4Desc: Decision review; file a request for re-interview or IJ review if needed.
credible-fear-interview.step5Desc: If passed: transition to full affirmative/defensive asylum engagement.

bond-hearing.title: Bond Hearing
bond-hearing.short: Get your loved one released from ICE detention.
bond-hearing.headline: 48 hours out beats 48 months in.
bond-hearing.forms: Bond motion, sponsor affidavits, evidence of ties
bond-hearing.overview1: A bond hearing is where an immigration judge decides whether to release a person from ICE custody while their removal case proceeds. The judge looks at flight risk, danger to the community, and community ties.
bond-hearing.overview2: Preparation is everything. We gather proof of address, employment, family ties, tax records, clean criminal history, U.S. citizen/LPR relative support, sponsor affidavits, and community letters. We present a full picture — not just a request.
bond-hearing.overview3: Most of our detained clients are released within 2–4 weeks of engagement. Bond amounts vary by case; we negotiate where possible and file custody redeterminations when bond is denied initially.
bond-hearing.step1Desc: Same-day intake. Identify the facility, pull A-file, start evidence collection.
bond-hearing.step2Desc: Sponsor affidavits, community letters, tax returns, leases, employment verification.
bond-hearing.step3Desc: File the motion with the immigration court serving the facility.
bond-hearing.step4Desc: We present evidence and argue for the lowest appropriate bond or release on OR.
bond-hearing.step5Desc: Guide the family through bond payment (ICE) and release logistics.

bond-deportation-package.title: Bond + Deportation Defense Package
bond-deportation-package.short: All-in-one engagement: bond, release, and full removal defense.
bond-deportation-package.headline: One team. One fee. Start to finish.
bond-deportation-package.overview1: This package combines the bond fight and the removal defense into a single engagement. You get coordinated strategy, no handoff gaps, and a single written fee covering both phases.
bond-deportation-package.overview2: It's designed for families dealing with a detained loved one who also wants a dedicated defense team for the underlying removal case. Most clients start here when ICE custody is involved.
bond-deportation-package.overview3: We handle bond, transfer monitoring if ICE moves the client, and every stage of the removal case through final hearing and appeal.
bond-deportation-package.step2Desc: Bond granted or custody redetermined; coordinate release logistics.
bond-deportation-package.step3Desc: Identify every form of relief (cancellation, asylum, adjustment, withholding, CAT).
bond-deportation-package.step4Desc: Evidence gathering, mock hearings, witness and expert prep.
bond-deportation-package.step5Desc: Full merits representation, with BIA appeal included if needed.

bond-habeas.title: Bond + Habeas Corpus
bond-habeas.short: Federal habeas petition for clients held beyond statutory limits.
bond-habeas.headline: When ICE holds you past the law, we go to federal court.
bond-habeas.forms: 28 U.S.C. § 2241 petition, evidence of prolonged detention
bond-habeas.overview1: Some detention is unlawful — mandatory detention that's gone on too long, post-order detention past the Zadvydas six-month mark, or detention without a bond hearing at all. Federal habeas relief can force release.
bond-habeas.overview2: We combine a bond filing (when available) with a federal habeas petition to attack the detention on multiple fronts simultaneously.
bond-habeas.overview3: These are complex cases with short windows. We move fast and we don't take them unless we can build a real record.
bond-habeas.step1Desc: Review custody history, statutory basis, and Zadvydas/Demore posture.
bond-habeas.step2Desc: File a bond motion with the immigration court if a bond hearing is available.
bond-habeas.step3Desc: File a habeas petition in the appropriate U.S. District Court.
bond-habeas.step4Desc: Draft reply brief; oral argument where set.
bond-habeas.step5Desc: Court-ordered release with conditions, or remand for a bond hearing.

bia-appeal.title: BIA Appeal
bia-appeal.short: Appeal an immigration judge's decision to the Board of Immigration Appeals.
bia-appeal.headline: The judge's decision isn't the last word.
bia-appeal.overview1: If an immigration judge denies your relief, you have 30 days to file a Notice of Appeal with the BIA. Missing the deadline is fatal. Timing, filing, and framing the legal issues correctly are everything.
bia-appeal.overview2: BIA appeals are won or lost in the legal brief. We identify reversible errors, preserve issues for federal court review, and write briefs that read like federal appellate work.
bia-appeal.overview3: We also take over mid-appeal when an existing brief is underdeveloped or when another attorney missed the deadline.
bia-appeal.step1Desc: Obtain the full administrative record and transcript.
bia-appeal.step2Desc: Identify legal and factual errors preserved for review.
bia-appeal.step3Desc: Full appellate brief with record citations.
bia-appeal.step4Desc: File on time; reply to DHS brief where allowed.
bia-appeal.step5Desc: If remanded: back to IJ. If denied: petition for review at the circuit court.

motion-to-reopen.title: Motion to Reopen
motion-to-reopen.short: Reopen a case based on new evidence, ineffective assistance, or changed country conditions.
motion-to-reopen.headline: New facts deserve a new look.
motion-to-reopen.overview1: A motion to reopen asks the court to reconsider a prior decision based on material facts that weren't available before. Common grounds: ineffective assistance of counsel, changed country conditions, new qualifying relative.
motion-to-reopen.overview2: Deadlines and numerical limits apply (generally one motion within 90 days), with statutory exceptions for certain grounds. Filing the right motion on the right schedule is critical.
motion-to-reopen.overview3: We evaluate quickly, gather the supporting evidence, and file a tightly-argued motion with the legal framework the adjudicator needs to grant.
motion-to-reopen.step1Desc: Assess the legal ground and whether a time/number exception applies.
motion-to-reopen.step2Desc: Affidavits, new evidence, country reports, expert reports if applicable.
motion-to-reopen.step3Desc: Fact and law sections with careful record citations.
motion-to-reopen.step4Desc: File with court or BIA; reply to DHS opposition.
motion-to-reopen.step5Desc: Reopening granted: back to hearing. Denied: federal review options.

motion-to-terminate.title: Motion to Terminate
motion-to-terminate.short: Terminate removal proceedings when the NTA is defective or relief is granted elsewhere.
motion-to-terminate.headline: Sometimes the best defense is no case at all.
motion-to-terminate.overview1: Termination ends the removal case. Grounds include defective Notices to Appear (Niz-Chavez issues), prosecutorial discretion, or pending USCIS relief that makes continued proceedings inappropriate.
motion-to-terminate.overview2: DHS can oppose or join. We prepare the motion, coordinate with the OPLA prosecutor, and push for termination or administrative closure where termination is unavailable.
motion-to-terminate.overview3: For clients with strong equities and no removability issue, termination is often a cleaner path than fighting for relief in court.
motion-to-terminate.step1Desc: Assess the NTA for defects and check eligibility for USCIS relief.
motion-to-terminate.step3Desc: File the motion with supporting brief and evidence.
motion-to-terminate.step4Desc: Oral argument if the court sets one.
motion-to-terminate.step5Desc: Termination, administrative closure, or denial — next steps prepared for each.

change-of-venue.title: Change of Venue
change-of-venue.short: Move your immigration court case to a court closer to where you live.
change-of-venue.headline: You shouldn't have to cross three states for a hearing.
change-of-venue.forms: Motion to change venue, address evidence
change-of-venue.overview1: If you've moved since your case was filed, a change of venue motion moves your case to the court that serves your new address. Getting venue right matters: judge patterns, scheduling, and logistics all change by court.
change-of-venue.overview2: This is usually an add-on service combined with a full engagement, but can be a standalone filing where the client already has counsel handling the merits.
change-of-venue.overview3: We handle notification to ICE OPLA, address evidence, and follow-up confirmation that the transfer actually completed.
change-of-venue.step1Desc: Collect lease, utility bills, and other address proof.
change-of-venue.step2Desc: Draft the motion with legal basis and good cause.
change-of-venue.step3Desc: File with the current court and serve on OPLA.
change-of-venue.step4Desc: Confirm the case actually moves to the new court.
change-of-venue.step5Desc: Confirm new Master Calendar date and prepare accordingly.

circuit-appeal.title: Petition for Review (Circuit Court)
circuit-appeal.short: Federal appellate review of a final BIA order.
circuit-appeal.headline: Federal court is the last honest look your case gets.
circuit-appeal.forms: Petition for review, appellate brief, record
circuit-appeal.overview1: If the BIA affirms a denial, you have 30 days to file a petition for review in the federal circuit court covering where the immigration judge sat. Federal judges review for legal and constitutional errors.
circuit-appeal.overview2: These cases require federal appellate skill — record citations, legal framing, and argument in open court before a three-judge panel. We brief them like the federal appeals they are.
circuit-appeal.overview3: Rafael is admitted to the Eleventh Circuit. For cases in other circuits we associate with admitted local counsel.
circuit-appeal.step1Desc: Obtain and read the entire administrative record.
circuit-appeal.step2Desc: Legal errors, due process, constitutional issues.
circuit-appeal.step3Desc: Fully briefed with standards of review, argument, and conclusion.
circuit-appeal.step4Desc: If the court grants argument, prep and present.
circuit-appeal.step5Desc: If remanded: back to BIA/IJ. Further review via Supreme Court rare but considered.

habeas-corpus.title: Habeas Corpus
habeas-corpus.short: Federal habeas for unlawful detention beyond statutory bounds.
habeas-corpus.headline: Unlawful detention has a federal remedy.
habeas-corpus.forms: 28 U.S.C. § 2241 petition, evidence of prolonged detention
habeas-corpus.overview1: Federal habeas under 28 U.S.C. § 2241 can challenge the legality of ICE detention when removal is not reasonably foreseeable (Zadvydas), when mandatory detention is prolonged (Demore/Jennings), or when a bond hearing was improperly denied.
habeas-corpus.overview2: Habeas petitions are filed in the U.S. District Court where the detainee is held. We draft the petition, coordinate service on the government, and argue the motion to release.
habeas-corpus.overview3: Not every prolonged detention qualifies. We evaluate realistically and only take cases where there's a viable legal theory.
habeas-corpus.step1Desc: Review custody history and statutory basis.
habeas-corpus.step2Desc: Draft habeas petition with declarations and exhibits.
habeas-corpus.step3Desc: File in the appropriate district court; serve DHS/ICE.
habeas-corpus.step4Desc: Review government brief; file reply and any amended petition.
habeas-corpus.step5Desc: Court-ordered release, bond hearing, or denial — appeal ready if needed.

family-petitions.title: Family-Based Petitions (I-130)
family-petitions.short: I-130 filings for spouses, parents, children, and siblings of U.S. citizens and LPRs.
family-petitions.headline: The paperwork that keeps families under one roof.
family-petitions.timeline: Immediate relatives: 8–16 months. Preference categories: variable.
family-petitions.overview1: The I-130 is the foundation of most family immigration cases. It establishes a qualifying relationship between a U.S. citizen or LPR petitioner and a foreign national beneficiary.
family-petitions.overview2: Our I-130 work focuses on proving bona fides decisively: joint financial records, photographs over time, affidavits from people who know both spouses, travel records, and evidence of shared life.
family-petitions.overview3: Adjustment of status (I-485) is a separate engagement, but we frequently bundle them for clients already in the U.S.
family-petitions.step1Desc: Gather certificates, photos, joint accounts, affidavits, proof of cohabitation.
family-petitions.step2Desc: Complete the form with careful accuracy.
family-petitions.step3Desc: File with USCIS with all supporting evidence.
family-petitions.step4Desc: Respond promptly to Requests for Evidence if USCIS issues one.
family-petitions.step5Desc: Receive I-130 approval; proceed to I-485 adjustment or consular processing.

adjustment-of-status.title: Adjustment of Status (I-485)
adjustment-of-status.short: Green card application for eligible beneficiaries inside the U.S.
adjustment-of-status.headline: From paperwork to permanent residence.
adjustment-of-status.overview1: Adjustment of status lets eligible people already in the U.S. become lawful permanent residents without leaving the country. It's paired with an approved (or pending) I-130 and requires a medical exam and affidavit of support.
adjustment-of-status.overview2: The I-485 is straightforward when there are no admissibility issues. We flag and resolve anything that could trigger an RFE or a denial before filing.
adjustment-of-status.overview3: EAD and Advance Parole are usually filed concurrently so you can work and travel during processing.
adjustment-of-status.step1Desc: Confirm priority date, check grounds of inadmissibility, plan for waivers if needed.
adjustment-of-status.step2Desc: I-864 from petitioner, joint sponsor if required, tax transcripts.
adjustment-of-status.step3Desc: Civil surgeon appointment and sealed I-693.
adjustment-of-status.step4Desc: I-485 with I-765 and I-131 concurrently.
adjustment-of-status.step5Desc: USCIS interview (most couples case) with our attorney present.

family-package.title: Family Package (I-130 + I-485 + EAD)
family-package.short: The complete family-based green card journey, bundled.
family-package.headline: One plan. One flat fee. Green card at the end.
family-package.overview1: This package combines the I-130 petition, the I-485 adjustment, and the I-765 EAD application into a single engagement — the path most family-based green card cases actually take.
family-package.overview2: You get predictable pricing, a single point of contact, and coordinated filings. We file everything concurrently where eligible and prep you for a single combined USCIS interview.
family-package.overview3: Most of our family-based clients choose this package. It's the cleanest path from 'filing date' to 'green card in hand.'
family-package.step2Desc: Relationship bona fides, medical, financial, identity documents.
family-package.step3Desc: I-130, I-485, I-765, I-131 filed together.
family-package.step4Desc: Biometrics at ASC; EAD typically arrives in 3–6 months.
family-package.step5Desc: Interview with our attorney; green card issued after approval.

provisional-waiver.title: Provisional Waiver (I-601A)
provisional-waiver.short: Waiver of unlawful presence before consular processing abroad.
provisional-waiver.headline: File here. Interview home. Come back approved.
provisional-waiver.overview1: The I-601A provisional waiver lets certain applicants file for a waiver of unlawful presence before leaving the U.S. for consular processing. Approved in the U.S., you travel for the interview, and return approved.
provisional-waiver.overview2: The case hinges on proving extreme hardship to a U.S. citizen or LPR spouse or parent if you were barred from returning. Medical, financial, educational, and country-conditions evidence all contribute.
provisional-waiver.overview3: We prepare hardship cases with the same care as cancellation cases — full evidence, expert declarations where useful, and a narrative that reads as a single coherent story.
provisional-waiver.step1Desc: Confirm qualifying relative and absence of disqualifying issues.
provisional-waiver.step2Desc: Medical, financial, educational, country-conditions, psychological evaluation.
provisional-waiver.step3Desc: Submit the provisional waiver package to USCIS.
provisional-waiver.step4Desc: On approval, proceed to consular processing (DS-260) at the home-country consulate.
provisional-waiver.step5Desc: Interview at the consulate; return with immigrant visa.

vawa.title: VAWA Self-Petition (I-360)
vawa.short: Immigration relief for abused spouses, children, and parents of U.S. citizens or LPRs.
vawa.headline: Your abuser does not control your immigration status.
vawa.overview1: The Violence Against Women Act lets abused spouses, children, and parents of U.S. citizens or LPRs petition for their own immigration status — without the abuser's knowledge, signature, or involvement.
vawa.overview2: Confidentiality is absolute. VAWA files are treated under special protections; your abuser cannot obtain any information about the filing. We correspond through the address you specify.
vawa.overview3: Strong VAWA cases are built on the personal statement, corroborated by police reports, medical records, photographs, counselor notes, and affidavits from people who witnessed the relationship.
vawa.step1Desc: Confidential consultation, safety planning, case eligibility review.
vawa.step2Desc: Personal statement, police/medical records, photos, witness affidavits.
vawa.step3Desc: File the self-petition with full evidence package.
vawa.step4Desc: On prima facie determination, file I-485 and I-765 when eligible.
vawa.step5Desc: I-360 approval; adjustment of status to LPR.

u-visa.title: U-Visa
u-visa.short: Immigration relief for victims of serious crimes who cooperate with law enforcement.
u-visa.headline: What happened to you was not your fault. You have rights.
u-visa.timeline: 5–8 years to visa; 4+ years for work permit
u-visa.overview1: The U-Visa is available to noncitizen victims of qualifying crimes (domestic violence, sexual assault, felonious assault, human trafficking, and others) who have suffered substantial harm and have been, are, or are likely to be helpful to law enforcement.
u-visa.overview2: The case requires a law enforcement certification (I-918B) from the investigating agency. We coordinate with local prosecutors, victim advocates, and detectives to secure the certification.
u-visa.overview3: Current waitlist is long, but applicants on the waitlist receive deferred action and work authorization after 4+ years. This is life-changing relief for survivors.
u-visa.step1Desc: Confirm qualifying crime, assess safety, plan confidentiality.
u-visa.step2Desc: Coordinate with law enforcement to obtain I-918B.
u-visa.step3Desc: Personal statement, medical/mental health evaluations, corroborating evidence.
u-visa.step4Desc: Work authorization and deferred action while on waitlist.
u-visa.step5Desc: Grant when visa number available; adjust to LPR three years later.

work-permit.title: Work Permit (I-765)
work-permit.headline: Work legally while your case is pending.
work-permit.overview1: The I-765 Employment Authorization Document (EAD) lets eligible applicants work legally in the U.S. Eligibility categories vary — asylum applicants, adjustment applicants, DACA recipients, U-visa waitlist, VAWA, and more.
work-permit.overview2: We identify the correct eligibility category, prepare the application, and track biometrics and approval.
work-permit.overview3: EADs typically arrive in 3–6 months. Renewals can be filed up to 180 days before expiration, with automatic 540-day extensions in many categories.
work-permit.step1Desc: Determine which eligibility category applies to your situation.
work-permit.step3Desc: Submit I-765 to USCIS with correct filing fee (or fee waiver).
work-permit.step4Desc: Attend biometrics appointment at ASC if required.

work-permit-addon.title: Work Permit (Add-On)
work-permit-addon.short: Discounted I-765 add-on for clients with an existing case.
work-permit-addon.headline: Work permit, bundled with your case.
work-permit-addon.overview1: When we're already handling your underlying case (asylum, adjustment, VAWA, etc.), adding an I-765 work permit is a small, flat add-on fee. Same preparation standard, lower overhead.
work-permit-addon.overview2: This service is only available to existing Verde Law clients with an active case. It cannot be purchased standalone.
work-permit-addon.overview3: Renewals receive the same discounted add-on pricing while the underlying case is pending.
work-permit-addon.step1Desc: Confirm category and that the underlying case is still active.
work-permit-addon.step5Desc: Calendar renewal window; refile before expiration.

naturalization.title: Naturalization (N-400)
naturalization.short: U.S. citizenship application, interview prep, and oath ceremony.
naturalization.headline: From green card to citizenship — the last step home.
naturalization.overview1: Naturalization is the path from lawful permanent residence to U.S. citizenship. Eligibility requires 5 years of LPR status (3 if married to a U.S. citizen), continuous residence and physical presence, good moral character, and basic English and civics.
naturalization.overview2: We screen for issues that can derail the application — failure to file taxes, extended absences abroad, criminal issues, selective service non-registration — and plan accordingly.
naturalization.overview3: We prep you for the English/civics test and conduct a mock interview before the real one.
naturalization.step1Desc: Residence, presence, character, tax, travel, and criminal screening.
naturalization.step2Desc: Complete N-400 with full trip history and supporting documents.
naturalization.step3Desc: File with USCIS; attend biometrics at ASC.
naturalization.step4Desc: Civics/English practice, mock interview, attorney present at the real interview.
naturalization.step5Desc: Take the oath and receive your Certificate of Naturalization.

green-card-renewal.title: Green Card Renewal (I-90)
green-card-renewal.short: Renew or replace a lawful permanent resident card.
green-card-renewal.headline: Renewal without the headache.
green-card-renewal.overview1: Green cards must be renewed every 10 years. The I-90 also covers replacements for lost, stolen, or damaged cards, and corrections for errors on existing cards.
green-card-renewal.overview2: We handle the filing, respond to any RFEs, and track approval through card delivery.
green-card-renewal.overview3: Consider filing for citizenship instead if eligible — we'll tell you if the N-400 makes more sense than a renewal.
green-card-renewal.step1Desc: Confirm category and that renewal (not N-400) is the right path.
green-card-renewal.step2Desc: Submit the form with supporting documents and fee.
green-card-renewal.step4Desc: Receive 24-month extension letter pending card production.
green-card-renewal.step5Desc: Receive new green card by mail.

foia-request.title: FOIA Request
foia-request.short: Obtain your A-file or case records from USCIS, ICE, or EOIR.
foia-request.headline: Know what the government has on you.
foia-request.overview1: Your A-file (alien file) contains everything the government has on file about your immigration history — prior applications, entries, detentions, notices, decisions. It's the baseline for any serious strategy decision.
foia-request.overview2: We file targeted FOIA requests, respond to any deficiency letters, and provide a written summary of what the records show.
foia-request.overview3: Useful before filing new applications, before consular processing, before criminal-immigration consultations, and in any case where the prior record matters.
foia-request.step1Desc: Identify which agency (or agencies) to request from.
foia-request.step2Desc: Submit signed FOIA requests to each agency.
foia-request.step3Desc: Follow up with agency FOIA offices as needed.
foia-request.step4Desc: Review and summarize the returned records.
foia-request.step5Desc: Use records to plan next-step filings.

rfe-response.title: RFE Response
rfe-response.short: Targeted response to a Request for Evidence from USCIS.
rfe-response.headline: One chance to answer. We get it right.
rfe-response.overview1: A Request for Evidence (RFE) is USCIS asking for more information before deciding a case. A strong RFE response can save an otherwise denied case. A weak one seals the denial.
rfe-response.overview2: We read the RFE carefully, identify exactly what USCIS is asking and why, gather the right documents, and draft a targeted legal response that addresses each concern head-on.
rfe-response.overview3: We take RFE responses even when we didn't file the underlying case — common when the original attorney dropped the ball or the client filed pro se.
rfe-response.step1Desc: Read the notice, identify the issues, and determine what's really being requested.
rfe-response.step2Desc: Collect every piece of documentation that addresses the RFE concerns.
rfe-response.step3Desc: Draft a legal cover letter and organize exhibits logically.
rfe-response.step4Desc: Submit within the deadline with tracking.
rfe-response.step5Desc: Track the case to final decision; plan for NOID or approval.

ice-checkin.title: ICE Check-In Representation
ice-checkin.short: Attorney representation at ISAP/ICE supervised check-ins.
ice-checkin.headline: You don't face ICE alone.
ice-checkin.overview1: ISAP and ICE check-ins vary in seriousness. Some are routine; others are ICE's opportunity to re-detain. Having an attorney present changes the posture of every interaction.
ice-checkin.overview2: We appear with you, monitor what's being asked, document any irregularities, and immediately escalate if ICE tries to take custody.
ice-checkin.overview3: This service is used heavily by clients with pending cases, prior orders, or recent check-in changes.
ice-checkin.step1Desc: Review your A-file and check-in history to anticipate ICE's posture.
ice-checkin.step2Desc: Ensure ICE has our appearance on file before the check-in.
ice-checkin.step3Desc: Attorney accompanies you to the appointment.
ice-checkin.step4Desc: Respond to any requests, resist any improper custody attempts.
ice-checkin.step5Desc: Written summary of what happened and next steps.
